content: 1. Dabigatran should not be coadministered with P-glycoprotein (P-gp) inhibitors in patients with atrial fibrillation if their creatinine clearance (CrCl) is less than 30 mL/min. For deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or pulmonary embolism (PE) treatment, avoid coadministration if CrCl is less than 50 mL/min. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 2. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of dabrafenib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Both itraconazole and dabrafenib prolong the QTc interval, necessitating avoidance or alternative therapy. 3. Danazol increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 4. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of daridorexant, darifenacin, and dasatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Additionally, itraconazole and these drugs may prolong the QTc interval, further supporting the need for alternative therapy. 5. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of darolutamide, a P-gp and CYP3A4 substrate. Close monitoring for adverse reactions is necessary, and darolutamide dosage should be adjusted when coadministered with strong or moderate P-gp and CYP3A4 inhibitors. 6. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of darunavir/ritonavir. When coadministered, itraconazole should not exceed 200 mg/day. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 7. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of dasatinib and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of daunorubicin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Deferasirox decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of deflazacort, a P-gp and CYP3A4 substrate. Reduce the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 and/or P-gp inhibitors. Monitor closely. 11. Itraconazole and degarelix both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Itraconazole and desflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Itraconazole and desipramine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Itraconazole and deutetrabenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. However, certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. 15. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of dexamethasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. DHEA (herbal) increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 18. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of diazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease the rate of diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 19. Didanosine decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer didanosine 2 hours before or several hours after itraconazole administration. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for potential adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 21. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of digoxin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Measure digoxin levels before initiating concomitant drugs. Monitor closely and consider reducing the digoxin dose by approximately 30-50% or modifying the dosing frequency. 22. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated due to the increased risk of ergotism, which can lead to cerebral ischemia and/or ischemia of the extremities. 23. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of diltiazem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Calcium channel blockers (CCBs) have negative inotropic effects that may be additive to those of itraconazole. Monitor for adverse reactions, and dose reduction of concomitant drugs may be necessary. 24. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of disopyramide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is contraindicated. 25. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of docetaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider a 50% dose reduction of docetaxel and monitor for increased toxicities. 26. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of dofetilide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is contraindicated. 27. Itraconazole and dolasetron both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Itraconazole and donepezil both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of doravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Itraconazole and doxepin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of doxorubicin by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-gp metabolism. Avoid use in combination with CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors due to the potential for increased systemic exposure and effects of doxorubicin. 32. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of dronabinol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of dronedarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is contraindicated. 34. Itraconazole and droperidol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 36. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of dutasteride by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor increases duvelisib AUC, which may increase the risk of toxicities. Reduce the duvelisib dose to 15 mg BID when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Monitor closely. 38. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, decrease the dose to 30 mg PO once daily. No dose reduction is recommended for NVAF. 39. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of elacestrant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than 1 month is not recommended. Elagolix decreases itraconazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and consider increasing CYP3A substrate doses if needed. 42. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Itraconazole increases the levels of eletriptan by decreasing its metabolism. Use of eletriptan within at least 72 hours of treatment with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is contraindicated. 44. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated with eliglustat in poor or intermediate metabolizers. Reduce the eliglustat dose in extensive metabolizers. Eliglustat and itraconazole both prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is contraindicated. 45. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of eluxadoline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism. 46. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. When coadministered, the itraconazole dose should not exceed 200 mg/day. Monitor closely. 47. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If concomitant use is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Itraconazole increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for signs of toxicities.
